newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Jan 24.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Friday:
* U.S. Attorney-General Janet Reno criticises the Saudi Arabian Government for failing to turn over important information in the investigation into the bombing that killed 19 Americans in Dhahran.
* Many Japanese are worried that their economy is at a critical juncture as the Tokyo stock market plunges and the yen continues its slide against the dollar.
* A panel of experts brought together by the National Institutes of Health have concluded there is no evidence that regular mammograms saves the lives of women in their 40s.
* New York police officers stage marches around the city to protest Mayor Rudolph Giuliani's latest wage contract offer.
* Central European nations move ahead toward prosperity and stability, leaving behind their poorer neighbours in Eastern Europe.
* The FBI arrests 32 in a sting to catch a mob-run million-dollar stolen goods ring.
* The increasingly belligerent cries for political independence by a small group in Texas worries federal and state officials.
